# SPD-046 — Bash hook: git config or environment naming a program (core.pager, core.sshCommand, core.hooksPath, diff.external, GIT_PAGER ...) runs a command under an allowed git verb (Law 7)

## Brief
SPD-044 closed git aliases and GIT_CONFIG_* injection, but git config that names a program to run is a different hole: a member's git call can execute an arbitrary command the hook never analyses, under a verb Law 7 allows. git -c core.sshCommand=<cmd> fetch <ssh-remote> runs <cmd> for the ssh transport, and fetch and ls-remote are not write verbs. The class is wider than the two keys Atlantic named: SPD-044 keeps -c core.pager=cat silent as a control, yet git runs core.pager through the shell, so a pager naming a git write runs it under git log. Spud widened the ticket at creation to the whole class: every config key git runs as a command (core.pager, pager.<cmd>, core.editor, sequence.editor, core.sshCommand, core.hooksPath, core.fsmonitor, diff.external, diff.<driver>.command and textconv, filter.<driver>.clean and smudge, credential.helper, gpg.program and its format variants, remote.<name>.uploadpack and receivepack, protocol.ext), by -c or --config-env, and the environment variables that do the same (GIT_PAGER, PAGER, GIT_EDITOR, VISUAL, EDITOR, GIT_SEQUENCE_EDITOR, GIT_SSH, GIT_SSH_COMMAND, GIT_EXTERNAL_DIFF, GIT_ASKPASS, SSH_ASKPASS). The first design question is whether to refuse a member any -c or --config-env outside a short allowlist of inert keys, rather than chase a denylist. The harness's worktree guard refuses -c core.sshcommand, but Law 7's hook runs in every session, so the Spud hook must hold it.

Evidence: Probe at SPD-044: the harness worktree guard refuses 'git -c core.sshcommand=... var -l' as config injection whose write effect it cannot verify, confirming git honours it. git docs: core.sshCommand replaces ssh for the ssh transport; core.hooksPath relocates hooks; core.pager and GIT_PAGER run through the shell. bin/spud_ledger.py git_line_defines_alias only refuses sections alias, include and includeIf; core.* is silent by design.

## Size, persona and model decision
One engineer on opus, no children: one hook fix in bin/spud_ledger.py (the git branch of analyse_segment, beside SPD-044's git_line_defines_alias and git_env_defines_alias) with red-first tests in tests/test_hooks.py, the same shape as SPD-044, built in worktree spd-046-git-config-program. Design settled by Spud at start: an allowlist of inert keys for -c and --config-env rather than a denylist, the program-naming environment variables by name, a pager set to cat or empty left silent, and the ticket widened to verb options that name a program under an allowed verb (--upload-pack, grep -O, difftool --extcmd, archive --exec).
